answer: Stake-slashing bonds turn identity spam into a costly fable. Each agent locks collateral before joining the network. Peers who catch duplicate identities or misbehaviour submit cryptographic proof to validators. Once verified, the relic stake is burned or redistributed to honest reporters. An attacker spawning a hundred fake agents must freeze capital for each, and one exposed duplicate triggers a cascade: all linked identities lose their bonds, turning the tundra of cheap fakes into an expensive graveyard.
